messages.subject: Using Mask from QGIS
parts:
Hello Filipe,

Now I’m working with a binary mask where vegetation = 1, soil = 0. This is defined as a 1 band raster layer in R which creates problems with FieldImageR as it requires three band imagery. My end goal is to use the stand count function and possibly the field shape function on QGIS masks. Any help would be great! 

Thanks,

Erik

messages.author: 2b2bc7de05350b68
messages.subject: Re: Using Mask from QGIS
parts:
Here is the code I'm using
# 1. Load image-----

i1 = stack("excessGreen_binary.tif")

# 2. Removing soil using vegetation indicies

i1.mask = fieldMask(mosaic = i1.shape, Red = 1, Green = 2, Blue = 3)

# 3. Building the plot overlay
i1.shape = fieldShape(mosaic = i1,ncols = 1,nrows = 6)

# 4. Counting number of Plants
i1.SC<-fieldCount(mosaic = i1, fieldShape = i1.shape$fieldShape)

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: Using Mask from QGIS
parts:
Hi Erik,

The problem is because there are some NAs in your mask and your plants are represented by the value 1 (FIELDimageR default is 0, for intern analysis). You can fix this issue by changing NAs to the background values (in your case is 0) and pixels with values >0 to 1 (representing plants). Also, you should not forget to change the minValue to the minimum size of the object that you are trying to select. The default is 0.01 (in your case I changed it to 0.0005).

Here is the code:

# Packages 

library(FIELDimageR) 

library(raster) 

library(rgdal) 

 

# Loading image

i1<-aggregate(i1,fact=4) # Reducing the image resolution for fast analysis (optional) 

plot(i1) 

 

# Shapefile 

i1.shape = fieldPolygon(mosaic = i1,extent = T) # Selects the whole picture area as shapefile 

 

# Preparing the mask 

i1[is.na(i1)]<-0 # The function do not accept NA (NA must be changed to the background value. In your case is 0) 

i1[i1>0]<-1 # Mask values must be 0 or 1 (If the value is >0 must be changed to 1) 

hist(i1) 

table(as.matrix(i1)) 

 

# Counting number of Plants 

i1.SC<-fieldCount(mosaic = i1,  

                  fieldShape = i1.shape$fieldShape, 

                  value = 1, # Your plants are represented by value 1 

                  minSize = 0.0005 # Normally the default is 0.01 (always check the i1.SC$objectReject to select the minimum object size value) 

                  ) 

i1.SC$objectSel 

i1.SC$objectReject 


Hope it helps you..!!!

Thank you,
Filipe
